author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating before claiming because the bead's recommended fix directly contradicts workspace policy.

The bead's Fix snippet shows:
```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct ChatFilterCondition {
    #[serde(flatten, default, skip_serializing_if = "serde_json::Map::is_empty")]
    pub extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
}
```
…but workspace AGENTS.md "Filter algebra and control enums are explicitly EXCLUDED" (decided 2026-05-10) says:
> Filter and comparator algebra types ... MUST NOT receive 'extra' fields or 'Other(String)' variants.
> Silent-drop is a server-side query-correctness bug.

The bead author was working off pre-policy assumptions. The correct shape is the mail-types template (EmailFilterCondition in crate-jmap-mail-types/src/query.rs:79–181): no 'extra: Map', plain Option<T> fields, doc block citing the filter-algebra exclusion.

Other risk dimensions before I commit:

1. **Scope is large.** This is 5 new FilterCondition structs (Chat, Message, Space, ChatContact, CustomEmoji — ReadPosition and SpaceInvite have no /query per draft §1180-1290), and likely 5 ComparatorProperty enums. Touches chat-types (new module), chat-server (5 type aliases + may need handler updates), chat-client (5 method signature changes), testjig (test reshaping).

2. **Per-object spec field lists** (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md):
   - Chat: kind (String), muted (Boolean)
   - Message: chatId, body (full-text), inThread, hasAttachment, hasMention, threadRootId, ...
   - Space: name (substring), isPublic (Boolean)
   - ChatContact: blocked (Boolean), presence (String)
   - CustomEmoji: spaceId (String, optional)
   Each needs editorial judgment about which spec fields appear in the typed struct and which are deferred.

3. **The malformed-operator hazard (workspace jmap-types/src/query.rs:75-100)** says the canonical mitigation is server-side filter validation, not type-level deny_unknown_fields. Adding typed FilterCondition structs is the right step but the silent-drop class isn't fully closed at the type level — the workspace already documents this. Worth noting on the close-comment that this bead lands the type-system half of the defense; the server-side validation half is separate.

**Recommendation: (a) do the work using the mail-types template, ignoring the bead's 'Note' suggesting extra: Map.**

I'd file the work as one epic with 5 children (one per chat object × FilterCondition+Comparator), so each can ship and be reviewed independently. Filing 'human' rather than autonomously starting because:
- The bead body's recommended shape contradicts policy. Even though policy is clear and my recommendation is unambiguous, this is a substantive workspace-architectural addition (5+5 new public types across 3 crates) and the high-stakes carve-out in 'When NOT to file human' rule 3 ('public API breaking') applies.
- Whether to do all 5 in one pass or to break into a multi-bead epic is a project-shaping decision rather than a coding decision.

The human action needed: confirm (a) use mail-types template (no extra: Map), and (b) whether to land this as a single bead or restructure as a 5-child epic.
